samples.summary: Bundles at least three unrelated workstreams in one change: OAuth CSRF/PKCE/consent hardening (backend + CLI), a brand-new access-log redaction module (`logSafeUrl`, including share-link path redaction unrelated to login), and the CLI error-envelope `command` attribution rework the tests attribute to a different issue (#661, touching ~20 CLI files), plus a frontend login-error banner. No originating issue text accompanies this review, but the in-tree evidence (test comments citing `#661`, and `docs/design/cli.md` §8.1 already specifying `command` before this diff) indicates the CLI envelope work is a separate, pre-existing spec item folded into an auth-hardening change. Bundling makes the auth change hard to review and hard to revert independently.

Deliberate, undiscussed compatibility breaks bundled into a hardening change: (a) `nonce` and `code_challenge` become hard requirements on `GET /auth/github?mode=cli`, so every already-released CLI gets a 400 and can no longer log in with no version negotiation; (b) `?mode=cli` is now refused outright on any non-loopback plain-http origin, so self-hosted http deployments lose CLI login entirely. Both are documented in cli.md/rest-api.md/backend.md as intentional, but they are product-level breaks beyond "add PKCE + state binding" and deserve to be an explicit, separately-approved decision rather than a side effect.

Design-doc discipline: the backend now redirects failed browser callbacks to `FRONTEND_URL/login?error=login_state` and the frontend login form grows an error-banner contract keyed on `?error=` values, but `docs/design/frontend.md` (the canonical frontend doc, §Login page at line 402 and the auth-flow list) is not updated. Only backend.md/rest-api.md record the new query contract, so the frontend side of a cross-package contract is undocumented in its own subsystem doc.

Duplication of a constant-time comparison helper: `secretEquals` is defined privately in `cli-auth.store.ts` and again (exported) in `github-auth.guard.ts` in the same directory, while `yorkie-signature.guard.ts` already hand-rolls the same length-check + `timingSafeEqual` pattern, and the CLI adds a third copy as `nonceMatches`. The repo expects reuse of shared helpers; the store could import the guard's exported `secretEquals` (or both could live in a small shared util).

Layer fit: the CLI consent interstitial is a full styled HTML page (inline markup + hand-written CSS with its own colours, shadows and typography) embedded in `AuthController`. UI is the frontend package's responsibility and the repo has a design-system unification doc; this introduces a second, unstyled-by-the-design-system UI surface with no template/view layer in the backend and a hand-rolled `escapeHtml` (a third copy of that helper, alongside `packages/board/src/import/miro/map-items.ts` and notes' markdown-it `escapeHtml`). A minimal unstyled page, or a frontend-hosted confirm route, would fit the existing layering better.

`docs/design/cli.md` Non-Goals still lists "Device flow or headless authentication (may be added later)", yet this change adds an explicit headless affordance (`~/.wafflebase/login-url.txt`, written 0600 when stderr is not a TTY, plus a documented file-tree entry). Either the Non-Goal should be narrowed to "device flow" or the new headless path acknowledged there, so the doc does not contradict the shipped behaviour.

Doc inconsistency introduced by the new one-line envelope rule: §9 now mandates a single line per error and the §7 USAGE example was reflowed accordingly, but the §8.1 canonical envelope example (docs/design/cli.md lines 887-895) is still shown pretty-printed across multiple lines.
Typo in the new risk-table row: "A `mode=cli' start" uses a mismatched backtick/apostrophe, so the inline code span does not render.

No originating issue text accompanies this review, but the in-tree evidence (test comments citing `#661`, and `docs/design/cli.md` §8.1 already specifying `command` before this diff) indicates the CLI envelope work is a separate, pre-existing spec item folded into an auth-hardening change. verdict.reason: The code exists (formatter.ts:58-161 has commandPath/errorEnvelope/backendErrorEnvelope; packages/backend/src/logging/log-safe-url.ts exists), so the bundling is factually real — but it is not a fit violation under this lens's major triggers, and the "unrelated workstreams" framing is contradicted by in-tree specs. (1) #661 is the branch's ORIGINATING issue, with its own plan and acceptance criteria in docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md:1-3,56-62, all met by formatter.ts; the pre-existing docs/design/cli.md:882,1156 (§8.1/§9) spec is what #661 implements — conformance, not creep. (2) logSafeUrl is not unrelated to login: it is acceptance criterion 20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:126-127 and plan bullet lines 78-89 (keep the nonce/code_challenge-bearing auth URL out of access logs), with the share-link token extension as review-round-2 criterion lines 154-156; the frontend login-error banner is round-2 criterion lines 157-159. (3) The branch sharing is explicitly recorded and justified at 20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:24-30 ("It rides the #661 branch again (PR #786)... the two touch login.ts from opposite ends"). (4) Design-doc discipline is satisfied in canonical subsystem docs, not parallel files: backend.md:427-432 for logSafeUrl, cli.md:177-302 for the nonce/PKCE/consent flow. The finding cites no failed acceptance criterion, no exceeded Non-Goal, no missing/parallel design doc, and no duplicated module; its residual claim is PR-splitting/reviewability hygiene, which the rubric classes as a minor preference that never blocks.

Both are documented in cli.md/rest-api.md/backend.md as intentional, but they are product-level breaks beyond "add PKCE + state binding" and deserve to be an explicit, separately-approved decision rather than a side effect.

verdict.reason: The code exists (github-auth.guard.ts:297-301 refuses ?mode=cli off loopback on plain http; :319-332 hard-400s missing/malformed nonce and code_challenge), but the finding's defect claim — that these are "undiscussed" breaks "beyond" the issue that arrived as a "side effect" — is not present in the repo record. (a) Requiring nonce + code_challenge is a literal acceptance criterion of the originating issue: docs/tasks/active/20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:121-123 ("A CLI that sends neither parameter is refused with a 400 naming the missing one (replaces the earlier criterion, which asked for behavior that left the binding optional and therefore absent)") and :130-133 ("fails closed … it does not complete … this replaces the earlier criterion, which asked for behavior that would reopen the hole"), with plan bullet :55-61 stating "Back-compat runs neither way now — an older CLI upgrades, or uses --api-key". So the guard satisfies the spec rather than exceeding it. (b) The non-loopback-http refusal is an explicitly deliberated decision recorded in the same task's review round 3: lessons.md:124-133 ("either the feature degrades with it (here: ?mode=cli is a 400 off loopback) or the degradation is the feature's real security level"). Against this lens's major rubric: no acceptance criterion is unmet; no design doc is missing or parallel (folded into the canonical backend.md:115-141, rest-api.md:334-359, cli.md:250-273/300-310); no stated Non-Goal is exceeded (cli.md:55-77 and todo.md:95-112 Out-of-scope cover neither client back-compat nor http deployments); nothing is duplicated. What is left is a process/approval preference ("should have been separately approved"), which the rubric fixes at minor and which never blocks.
